positiveFlows.title: THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ESTABLISH A COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROGRAM BETWEEN THE UNIVERSITY OF IOWA (UI), PACIFIC NORTHWEST NATIONAL LABORATORY (PNNL), AND LOS ALAMOS NATIONAL LABORATORY (LANL) AND TO CREATE A FORUM WITHIN WHICH GRADUATE STUDENTS GAIN EXPERTISE IN NUCLEAR AND RADIOCHEMICAL SCIENCES UNDER THE DIRECT MENTORSHIP OF UNIVERSITY AND NATIONAL LABORATORY INVESTIGATORS. THIS PROSPECT IS SIGNIFICANT AND WILL EXPAND THE RECRUITING POOL AVAILABLE TO THE NATIONAL LABORATORY SYSTEM WHILE ALSO STRATEGICALLY ADVANCING EFFORTS AT UI TO BUILD A NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED NUCLEAR AND RADIOCHEMISTRY PROGRAM. THIS PROPOSAL SUPPORTS THE EXPERTISE DEVELOPMENT MISSION OF THE NTNFC BY ESTABLISHING A COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN UI, PNNL, AND LANL FOCUSED ON A SHARED SCOPE OF RESEARCH THAT INCLUDES THE PREPARATION AND SPECTROSCOPIC CHARACTERIZATION OF ACTINIDE OXIDES AND OXALATES (E.G., UO2, PU2(C2O4)3, PU(C2O4)2), AND THEIR PRECURSOR MATERIALS. THE SUPPORTED GRADUATE STUDENTS WILL LEAD THE SCIENTIFIC UNDERTAKINGS AND RECEIVE TRAINING IN NUCLEAR MATERIAL HANDLING TO DEVELOP NATIONALLY NEEDED SKILLSETS IN PROCESSING SCIENCE, SPECTROSCOPIC CHARACTERIZATION, AND FORENSICS SIGNATURE DISCOVERY. SPECIFICALLY, RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON UNDERSTANDING HOW CONTAMINANTS, FREE RADICALS, AND DECOMPOSITION PRODUCTS WITHIN ACTINIDE OXIDES OR OXALATES CAN GENERATE DISTINCT SPECTROSCOPIC SIGNATURES THAT PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO MATERIAL PROVENANCE, AGE, AND ENRICHMENT LEVEL.

RAPID AND ACCURATE ELEMENTAL SEPARATION IS CRUCIAL FOR ANALYZING NATIONAL TECHNICAL NUCLEAR FORENSICS (NTNF) DEBRIS SAMPLES. PNNL HAS DEVELOPED STATE-OF-THE-ART FLOWSHEETS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TOOLS FOR SEPARATING AND QUANTIFYING ACTINIDES, FISSION, AND ACTIVATION PRODUCTS AND SEVERAL INSTRUMENT DATA-TRANSLATION TOOLS TO IMPROVE REPORTING TIMELINES. TO OPTIMIZE PNNL SEPARATION SYSTEMS, WE WILL DEVELOP CHEMICAL AND THEORETICAL METHODS AND CODING TOOLS TO ACCELERATE NTNF SAMPLE ANALYSES. THIS PROJECT IS UNIQUE BECAUSE IT IS MULTIDISCIPLINARY  IT COMBINES SPECIALISTS IN RADIOCHEMISTRY AND THEORETICAL CALCULATIONS IN ASSOCIATION WITH NTNF EXPERTS AT PNNL. WE WILL DELIVER IMPACTFUL METHODOLOGIES FOR SEPARATING RELEVANT NTNF ELEMENTS USING EXPERIMENTAL RADIOANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES, TOOLS THAT CONVERT RAW INSTRUMENT DATA INTO REPORT-READY FORMATS USING CODES SUCH AS PYTHON, AND THERMOCHEMICAL DATA THAT WILL AID WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF AI TOOLS TO PREDICT SEPARATION SCHEMESTHESE THERMODYNAMIC DATA WILL BE QUANTIFIED USING THEORETICAL CALCULATIONS (DENSITY-FUNCTIONAL THEORY, DFT). WE WILL ALSO TRAIN TWO PH.D. AND TWO UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, WHO WILL GRADUATE WITH A SOPHISTICATED KNOWLEDGE OF CHEMICAL SEPARATIONS, RADIOANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES AND INSTRUMENTATION, CODING, AND THEORETICAL CALCULATIONS FOR PROBLEMS ASSOCIATED WITH NUCLEAR FORENSICS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL REACH OUT TO OTHER POTENTIAL STUDENTS, SPARKING THEIR INTEREST IN NUCLEAR FORENSICS AND DHS SCIENTIFIC ACTIVITIES. THIS APPLICATION RESPONDS TO THE NOFO TMA 3 THAT ASKS EXPLICITLY FOR INNOVATIONS THAT RAPIDLY IDENTIFY AND QUANTIFY ELEMENTAL AND ISOTOPIC CONSTITUENTS (MAJOR, MINOR, AND TRACE) IN FRESH RADIOACTIVE FALLOUT DEBRIS AND DATA HANDLING METHODOLOGIES. THIS WORK WILL SUBSTANTIALLY IMPACT 1) THE ACCELERATION OF NUCLEAR FORENSICS DATA PROCESSING AND REPORTING, 2) SEPARATION SCIENCE AND ASSOCIATED PREDICTIVE CAPABILITIES, 3) THE TRAINING OF THE NEXT GENERATION IN NU-CLEAR FORENSICS, AND 4) THE VISIBILITY OF THE DHS SCIENTIFIC ACTIVITIES TO THE US ACADEMIC COM-MUNITIES, THEREFORE SUPPORTING THE DHS COUNTERING WEAPONS OF MASS DESTRUCTION OFFICE (CWMD) MISSION OBJECTIVE TO DETECT NUCLEAR MATERIALS.

THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO INVESTIGATE THE RAMAN SIGNATURES OF TRANSITION METALS IN URANIUM DIOXIDE, A POTENTIAL COMPONENT OF A RADIOLOGICAL DISPERSE DEVICE (RDD), AND FOCUS ON THEIR DISTRIBUTION BETWEEN THE ORIGINAL MATERIAL AND EXPLOSION DEBRIS, LINKING THIS WAY PRE- AND POST-DETONATION FORENSICS. UNDERSTANDING HOW THESE TRANSITION METALS ARE DISTRIBUTED (FRACTIONATED) AND THEIR RAMAN SPECTRAL CHARACTERISTICS COULD BE INSTRUMENTAL IN DETERMINING THE ORIGIN AND HISTORY OF A RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL INVOLVED IN A POTENTIAL ACT OF TERRORISM OR RADIOLOGICAL DISPERSAL DEVICE INCIDENT. THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A SKILLED WORKFORCE IN THE CRITICAL FIELD OF NUCLEAR FORENSICS BY TRAINING STUDENTS IN ADVANCED ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES AND BY PROVIDING THEM WITH SPECIALIZED TRAINING IN ANALYZING MATERIALS RELATED TO NUCLEAR FORENSICS. COLLABORATION WITH OAK RIDGE NATIONAL LABORATORY WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS WITH HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE AND ALLOW THEM TO CONTRIBUTE DIRECTLY TO NATIONAL SECURITY EFFORTS THROUGH INTERNSHIPS AT ORNL. FURTHERMORE, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTE TO NUCLEAR-RELATED CURRICULUM ENHANCEMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CENTRAL FLORIDA. THE PROJECT ALIGNS WITH DHS OBJECTIVES BY CULTIVATING FUTURE LEADERS IN NUCLEAR FORENSICS, FOSTERING STRONG UNIVERSITY-LABORATORY PARTNERSHIPS, AND EXPANDING CAPABILITIES AT UCF, PARTICULARLY AS ONE OF THE NATION S LARGEST HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTIONS.

positiveFlows.title: WE PROPOSE TO USE THE GAMMA-GAMMA COINCIDENCE TECHNIQUE TO INCREASE THE SENSITIVITY OF GAMMA SPECTROMETRY AND TO SPATIALLY LOCALIZE FISSION PRODUCT SAMPLES WITHIN LARGE VOLUMES. THE COINCIDENCE METHOD IS WIDELY USED IN FUNDAMENTAL NUCLEAR STRUCTURE PHYSICS AND IS KNOWN TO SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIOS. THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF EMITTED GAMMA RAYS SHOULD ALSO ALLOW A SOURCE TO BE LOCATED WITHIN A LARGE SAMPLE, SO WE WILL CONSTRUCT LARGE SAMPLES ( 30-60 CM ON A SIDE) WITH EMBEDDED ACTIVITY TO TEST THIS APPROACH. OUR TEAM HAS ACCESS TO A SET OF UNIQUE NEUTRON-IRRADIATED URANIUM DIOXIDE SAMPLES THAT CAN BE USED AS FISSION PRODUCT SOURCES FOR THESE STUDIES. WE WILL ACQUIRE A SMALL NUMBER OF SINGLE-CRYSTAL GERMANIUM DETECTORS, AND THESE WILL BE AUGMENTED BY HIGH-EFFICIENCY CLOVER GERMANIUM DETECTORS ON LOAN FROM THE CLOVERSHARE COLLABORATION. THIS RESEARCH WILL BE HEAVILY SYNERGIZED BY UTILIZING EXPERTS IN NUCLEAR SPECTROSCOPY, RADIOCHEMISTRY, AND RADIATION DETECTION. OUR COLLABORATORS FROM PACIFIC NORTHWEST NATIONAL LABORATORY ALSO HAVE EXISTING EXPERTISE IN GAMMA-GAMMA COINCIDENCE MEASUREMENTS. THE TWO MAJOR OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW ANALYTICAL METHODS AND OPTIMIZED DETECTOR SETUPS AND THE TRAINING OF TWO GRADUATE STUDENTS IN DATA ANALYSIS AND RADIOCHEMICAL METHODS.
